topic.readerProblem: Verify that an AI citation audit handoff still contains the exact files, bytes, hashes, and internal IDs declared by its manifest.
topic.connection: Citation-evidence integrity supports reproducible review of the sources and answer records behind AEOeye-style brand citation audits.

assessment: The page ships a complete populated synthetic bundle, a deterministic valid report, and a validator that checks inventory integrity and citation-ID closure. It clearly separates byte integrity from truth, completeness, sampling quality, reviewer correctness, and live engine evidence.

sources.supports: The SHA-256 algorithm family used for the bundle's byte-integrity digests.
The provenance concepts used to describe artifacts, generating activities, and review handoffs.
The separate JSON canonicalization scheme cited when byte-stable JSON signatures are required.
The standard-library SHA-256 implementation used by the validator.
The standard-library filesystem path handling used by the validator.

checks: Ran the original bundle and byte-compared its valid three-file JSON report with expected-report.json.
Copied the bundle to a temporary directory, appended one byte to notes.txt, and confirmed exit code one plus a report that differs from the immutable baseline.

Reviewed manifest hashes, byte sizes, citation-ID closure, safe path handling, source claims, limitations, and all reader-accessible resource links; added reference-path validation and accurate image metadata.

artifacts.description: Dependency-free validator for manifest version, paths, inventory bytes, SHA-256, duplicates, and internal references.
Populated synthetic manifest with three file entries and one declared citation-ID relationship.
Two populated synthetic answer rows referencing the citation table.
Two populated synthetic citation rows with example-domain placeholder URLs.
Plain-text fixture scope disclosure included in the hashed manifest inventory.
Deterministic valid report used for byte-level baseline verification.
Baseline and tamper-test commands that preserve the published bundle and expected report.

methodology: The review recalculated every manifest file byte count and SHA-256 through the validator, checked citation-ID closure, compared the valid report bytes, ran a one-byte tamper test in a temporary copy, and tested a traversal-style reference so the validator rejects reference files outside the declared safe inventory.
limitations: Integrity checks cannot prove factual accuracy, source support, authorship, authorization, redaction, bundle completeness, unbiased sampling, or correct annotations; the fixture contains no live provider observations.
